clips.text: No, he didn't. There's no draft in here.
clips.script: [smooth, evasive] No, he didn't. [bland, denying] There's no draft in here.

clips.text: Go on, then. And Tom, if my gumbo isn't hot by six, I'm telling Bernadette it was your idea.
clips.script: [brisk, shooing] Go on, then. [sweet, menacing] And Tom, if my gumbo isn't hot by six, [firm, delighted] I'm telling Bernadette it was your IDEA.

clips.text: He's got it.
clips.script: [dry, fond, not looking] He's got it.

clips.text: No. Is it cold?
clips.script: [curt, then curious] No. [grudging, interested] Is it cold?

clips.text: Then I got here just in time.
clips.script: [grim, smug] Then I got here just in TIME.

clips.text: I tried. It was too hot. Before that it was too cold. I'd like to speak to whoever packed me.
clips.script: [tired, aggrieved] I tried. [fussy] It was too HOT. [peevish] Before that it was too COLD. [haughty, entitled] I'd like to speak to whoever packed me.

clips.text: I promise. I packed a ruler.
clips.script: [quiet, sincere] I promise. [dry, deadpan] I packed a RULER.

clips.text: She came by at seven to check on us. She called me the Other Tom and said my bowls were too close together.
clips.script: [mellow, easy] she came by at seven to check on us. [amused, laid-back] she called me the other tom and said my bowls were too close together.

clips.text: Thank you. Who's the lady behind you with the clipboard?
clips.script: [pleased, polite] Thank you. [curious, direct] Who's the lady behind you with the clipboard?

clips.text: And they're no good. Every flame on the street, and I still can't get warm. A fire's no use with nothing to bake.
clips.script: [weary, grudging] And they're no good. [low, frustrated] Every flame on the street, and I still can't get warm. [quiet, bitter] A fire's no use with nothing to bake.

clips.text: Write that down and sign it. Nobody on this street ever does.
clips.script: [brusque, pleased underneath] Write that down and sign it. [dry, grumbling] Nobody on this street ever does.

clips.text: There he is! Come here. Let me look at you. I missed that face. Now sit, you're having a muffin.
clips.script: [warm Long Island accent, bright, thrilled] There he is! Come here. Let me look at you. [warm Long Island accent, warm, plain] I missed that FACE. [warm Long Island accent, firm] Now sit, you're having a muffin.

clips.text: It's bigger than a BUS! It ate a boat!
clips.script: [shouting, delighted] It's bigger than a BUS! [certain, stating a fact] It ate a boat!

clips.text: Seven. And it never once came up at a block meeting.
clips.script: [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, dry, stunned] Seven. [older African American man, warm Louisiana drawl, wounded, pedantic] And it never once came up at a block meeting.

clips.text: The first one. Tom, you heard her.
clips.script: [thick New York accent, satisfied, pointing] The FIRST one. Tom, you heard her.

clips.text: It's an old building. They all do this. Have you tried a sweater?
clips.script: [slippery, landlord-like] It's an old building. They all do this. [breezy, unhelpful] Have you tried a sweater?

clips.text: Bernadette, your diagram had my gumbo behind the paper plates.
clips.script: [pointed, Creole warmth] Bernadette, your diagram had my gumbo behind the paper plates.

clips.text: Tom. A rosebush got sealed in orange glass, every stove on the block went out, and it was all fixed by six. I'd love a quote.
clips.script: [brisk, reporter] Tom. [rapid, delighted] A rosebush got sealed in orange glass, every stove on the block went out, and it was all fixed by six. [sweet, sharp] I'd love a QUOTE.

clips.text: Everyone got it. Then we moved the table.
clips.script: [dry, serene] Everyone got it. [calm, delighted] Then we moved the table.

clips.text: Fine. Have your fun. Keep it down after ten.
clips.script: [sullen, giving in] Fine. [grudging, petty] Have your fun. [muttering] Keep it down after TEN.
